validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE/CLASSIFICATION/ATTRIBUTION checked and confirmed. This is the historic Ukraine-Slovakia gas border crossing at Uzhhorod (Ukraine) / Veľké Kapušany (Slovakia) -- a real, well-documented international interconnection, not a GEM-only entity. Independent, non-GEM confirmation: (1) Eustream (Slovak TSO) 2014 press release on the inauguration of the reverse-flow 'Vojany-Uzhorod' pipeline, held at the Compressor Station in Veľké Kapušany; (2) Oxford Institute for Energy Studies 2018 paper listing 'Velké Kapušany (Ukraine-Slovakia)' as a named ENTSOG/IEA-tracked cross-border pipeline connection; (3) EP Power Europe's gas-transmission page describing Veľké Kapušany as 'the biggest compressor station in the EU', the entry/exit point 'to/from the natural gas transmission network in Ukraine'; (4) Eustream's 1-Jan-2025 press release on the halt of forward (Ukraine->Slovakia) flow at this exact entry point. Four independent origins (Eustream self-source, an academic/policy institute citing ENTSOG+IEA, an unrelated Czech energy group, and -- for the 2025 transit-halt context -- NPR) all describe the same physical crossing. CLASSIFICATION is correct (international gas transmission interconnector, not gathering/feeder). ATTRIBUTION is correct and matches the country-wide rule: Owner1 = Gas Transmission System Operator of Ukraine (the post-2020 TSOU entity, correctly NOT the pre-2020 Ukrtransgaz and NOT Gazprom) for the Ukrainian section, Owner2 = eustream for the Slovak section -- both independently confirmed as real, currently-operating entities at this crossing (eustream.sk self-source could not be cross-checked against tsoua.com for the GTSOU side because tsoua.com returns HTTP 403 to automated fetches -- gem.wiki's own citation of tsoua.com for the Owner1 name is plausible but I could not independently re-verify it in this pass; flag for a future pass with a different fetch path). STATUS: the sheet's 'operating' is CONFIRMED, with an important caveat -- Eustream's 1-Jan-2025 release confirms that scheduled/nominated FORWARD (transit) flow from Ukraine into Slovakia at this entry point stopped when the Gazprom-Naftogaz transit contract expired unrenewed (consistent with the country-wide Jan-2025 transit cessation), but Eustream explicitly states infrastructure-wide that 'the transmission of natural gas continues at all interconnection points in line with customer nominations' and that Eustream remains 'fully ready to fulfill its obligations and provide reliable transmission' -- i.e. the pipeline itself is NOT retired/mothballed, only the one flow direction/purpose (Russian transit) has zeroed out. Per the country-wide guidance, this is exactly the case where Status should stay 'operating' -- the asset remains in service (domestic use, and it is also the physical corridor for the EU->Ukraine reverse-flow imports that have run on this crossing since 2014/2020).

validity.recommendation: Verify whether Capacity=7062.93 MMcf/d (=200 mcm/d, converted from a round metric figure) and Diameter=1400mm describe ONE physical line or the AGGREGATE of the multi-line Uzhhorod/Veľké Kapušany crossing. Also cross-check against the 'Uzhhorod exit' duplicate cluster (P0780 / P1489 -- named in the orchestrator's scope guidance, outside this pass's 9-pipeline roster) and against the separately-named 'Vojany-Uzhhorod' reverse-flow interconnector (~10 bcm/y, built/upgraded 2014) at the cluster-adjudication pass. Do not apply a Capacity/Diameter/Length ref off this pass's evidence.
validity.researcher_notes: Independent sources describe the Uzhhorod<->Veľké Kapušany border crossing as a MULTI-LINE bundle, not a single 1400mm/14.5km pipe: EP Power Europe states the transmission system at Veľké Kapušany consists of 'four to five parallel pipelines mostly 48/56 inches in diameter' (=~1219mm/1422mm) operating at 7.35 MPa; the Oxford Institute for Energy Studies paper (citing ENTSOG and IEA data) gives the COMBINED capacity of the 'Velké Kapušany (Ukraine-Slovakia)' connection as 189.0 mmcm/d (ENTSOG) / 197.5 mmcm/d (IEA) = 69.0/72.1 bcm/y -- close to, but not identical to, GEM's 200 mcm/d (=73.03 bcm/y, itself a suspicious round-number metric-to-imperial conversion per the country-wide flag on this exact row). A separate press trail (Eustream 2014 inauguration release; The Moscow Times, 2 Sep 2014, 'Slovak Gas Pipeline Offers New Reverse Supply Route for Ukraine') names a DISTINCT, smaller asset: the 'Vojany-Uzhhorod interconnector', built/upgraded specifically for east-bound reverse flow, running 'from the Vojany power station near the Ukrainian border to the western Ukrainian town of Uzhgorod' with a stated capacity of 'up to 10 billion cubic meters... a year' (~27.4 mcm/d) -- an order of magnitude smaller than GEM's 200 mcm/d, and with a different Slovak-side endpoint name (Vojany, not Velke Kapusany, though the 2014 inauguration ceremony itself was held at the CS in Veľké Kapušany, so the two places are closely linked/adjacent within the same hub). I cannot resolve from open sources whether GEM's P3063 (1400mm / 14.5km / 200 mcm/d) is meant to represent: (a) the aggregate of the whole historic multi-line crossing (in which case the single 1400mm diameter and 14.5km length materially understate the true 4-5-line asset), (b) one representative line within that bundle (plausible: 1400mm rounds close to the stated 56in/1422mm class), or (c) is being conflated with the separate, much-lower-capacity 2014 Vojany-Uzhhorod reverse-flow line. The 14.5km length is at least geographically plausible (Uzhhorod to Veľké Kapušany is ~15-20km airline distance), so LENGTH is not flagged as wrong, only unverified at that precision. This is exactly the kind of ambiguity the orchestrator's scope guidance calls out for the 'Uzhhorod exit' family (P0780 / P1489 / P3063) -- flagging for the redundancy/cluster-adjudication pass rather than resolving unilaterally.

fills.researcher_notes: Eustream's 1-Jan-2025 release (Slovak TSO, official) states 'the transmission of natural gas continues at all interconnection points' at this exact border point even as the Russia-transit forward flow stopped -- direct confirmation the asset is in service, not retired. EP Power Europe (unrelated Czech energy group) independently describes the Veľké Kapušany compressor station in the present tense as 'the biggest compressor station in the EU', a live description of currently-operating infrastructure at the Ukraine entry/exit point. Two independent, non-GEM origins.
Both sources describe this crossing explicitly as natural-gas transmission infrastructure (a 'Gas Transmission' business line / 'zemný plyn' [natural gas] flow). No ambiguity.

Eustream's 2014 release places the reverse-flow inauguration event 'at the Compressor Station in Veľké Kapušany' as the Slovak-side node of the 'Vojany-Uzhorod' (i.e. Uzhhorod-side) connection; EP Power Europe independently confirms Veľké Kapušany is the entry/exit point 'to/from the natural gas transmission network in Ukraine', close to the Ukrainian-Slovak border. Both endpoints (Uzhhorod, Ukraine / Veľké Kapušany, Slovakia) corroborated by two independent, non-GEM sources.

summary: P3063 (Uzhgorod-Velke Kapusany, Ukraine-Slovakia border crossing) is a real, correctly-classified, correctly-attributed international gas interconnector -- existence, classification and owner (GTSOU/eustream, not Gazprom) all confirmed independently; Status=operating confirmed with the documented Jan-2025 transit-flow caveat. Added refs for Status, Fuel, Location (all high tier, 2 independent sources each). Flagged a SPEC concern (low tier, no ref proposed): Capacity=200 mcm/d and Diameter=1400mm may represent the aggregate of a 4-5-parallel-line border crossing rather than one pipe, and a separate ~10 bcm/y 'Vojany-Uzhhorod' reverse-flow line (built/upgraded 2014) may or may not be the same asset -- routed to the cluster-adjudication pass alongside the orchestrator-flagged Uzhhorod-exit family (P0780/P1489). Capacity, Diameter and Length remain UNRESOLVED (no ref added).
